item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Smaller and More Robotic — Tue Sep 1, 12:00 AM — Oakwood Village Library and Arts Centre
item.description: Throughout the month of September, the works of artist Jay Rangam are on display at Oakwood Village Library Arts Centre. Jay Rangam is an artist that lives and works in Toronto, Canada. He received his MFA from the Maryland Institute College of Art in 2021 and his BFA from OCAD University in 2019. He has exhibited in group shows in Toronto, Montreal, Baltimore and New York. My recent paintings from 2024 - 2025 begin with digitally combining drawings that I’ve used in previous bodies of work to create new images. Using the digital cartoon as a starting point for painting, the application of different materials and colours is intended to abstract the representational subject matter of the drawings, creating paintings that appear somewhat abstract while retaining traces of a relationship to the natural world. item.description: Do you need information about applying for Rent-Geared-to-Income Housing or assistance with your application? Join Margaret's Housing and Community Support Services staff for drop-in sessions on the 3rd Tuesday of each month, from 2-4pm. This session has been rescheduled from Tuesday, August 18 to Tuesday, September 1. item.title: Beyond the Model: Why Fabric IQ Is the Missing Layer for Enterprise AI — Fri Sep 4, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto AI projects rarely fail because of the model — they fail because the data foundation underneath is fragile: agents that relearn the business every time, metrics that contradict each other, and no clear lineage for how an answer was reached.
This session breaks down Fabric IQ, Microsoft’s semantic and ontology layer for enterprise data, in plain terms. We’ll cover how Semantic Models, Ontologies, and Agents work together to turn raw tables into governed, trusted business context — enabling natural language interaction, consistent definitions across teams, and explainable AI answers. Attendees will leave with a clear, jargon-free understanding of where Fabric IQ fits in the modern data and AI stack, and how to start experimenting with it.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Shipra Vyas — Sat Sep 5, 12:00 AM — Albion
item.description: Throughout the month of September, the works of artist Shipra Vyas are on display at Albion branch. Shipra Vyas is a Toronto-based artist whose work explores memory, place, and the everyday moments that shape identity. Working primarily in pencil and pastel, she builds layered, textured drawings that carry a reflective atmospheric quality. Her practice is informed by family life, travel, her Indo Canadian roots, and literary influences, drawing on these to create intimate studies of connection, transition, and belonging. Her work can also be found on Instagram at @littlesketchdiary. "This series of drawings is inspired by Caitlin Vernon’s debut poetry collection Hold On Until I Can Love You. Beginning with the book cover & illustrations, the project grew into a larger body of work exploring themes of early relationships, identity, and place. item.description: ​Pilot, adventurer and photographer, Lola Reid Allin, transports audiences to exotic destinations around the world from the comfort of their chairs. item.title: Movie Matinee: Some Like It Hot (1959) — Fri Sep 11, 2:00 PM — Forest Hill
item.description:
Join us for an afternoon screening of the 1959 classic Some Like It Hot ! “Billy Wilder’s zany cross-dressing comedy begins with a massacre – resembling the gangland St Valentine’s Day killings of 1929 – and ends with one of the most celebrated last lines in cinema history. Written in cahoots with the director’s new collaborator I.A.L. Diamond, Some Like It Hot ascends to inspired heights of silliness in-between, with Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon both on career-best form as dragged-up musicians hiding out with Sugar Kane’s girl band. Both the gangster story and the screwball antics hark back to Hollywood films of the 1930s, but Wilder’s outrageous and subversive play with gender was truly boundary pushing and helped lead to a loosening of censorship after United Artists released the film without certification.” – British Film Institute Runtime: 2 hours and 1 minute.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults
